argument_markdown:
Let X=M_{6,6} and let \bar X=\overline M_{6,6}. Both are smooth Deligne–Mumford stacks over Q, X has complex dimension d=3\cdot6-3+6=21, and \bar X is proper. Write j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X for the open immersion.

For a smooth variety or smooth Deligne–Mumford stack X with a smooth proper compactification \bar X whose complement is a normal-crossings divisor, Deligne's weight spectral sequence gives

W_kH^k(X;Q)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(j^*:H^k(\bar X;Q)\to H^k(X;Q)\bigr).

Indeed, the weight spectral sequence for the logarithmic de Rham complex has E_1^{-p,k+p}=H^{k-p}(D^{[p]};Q)(-p). Its p=0 term is H^k(\bar X;Q), while every p>0 term has weight k+p>k. Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures therefore identifies the weight-k subspace with the image of the p=0 edge map. Applying this with k=26 yields

W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^{26}(\bar X;Q)\to H^{26}(X;Q)\bigr).  (1)

We now identify this image. A degree-26 class on \bar X that survives on X has codimension 13. The boundary-stratum filtration of \bar X is indexed by stable graphs. Its Gysin spectral sequence is compatible with the weight spectral sequence above. In total degree 26 and weight 26, only classes of Hodge bidegree (13,13) can contribute to the p=0 edge image: a summand of bidegree (a,b) with a+b=26 and a\ne b restricts to a class of the same unequal bidegree on X and hence would give a non-Tate summand of the lowest-weight piece. Such a summand cannot occur in the p=0 edge image here, because the degree-26 edge complex is the codimension-13 stable-graph complex: its generators are products of cotangent-line classes and fundamental classes of gluing strata, and its differential is the alternating sum of algebraic Gysin maps. Every generator is an algebraic cycle of codimension 13, hence has Hodge type (13,13) and spans Q(-13); every differential is a morphism of Tate Hodge structures. Kernels, images, and quotients in this finite complex are consequently direct sums of Q(-13). The edge image in (1), being a subquotient of that complex, is therefore a direct sum of Q(-13). Thus, for some cardinal r,

W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)\cong Q(-13)^{\oplus r}.  (2)

Finally, Poincare duality for the smooth 21-dimensional stack X gives

W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q)\cong W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21).

Twisting (2) by Q(21) sends Q(-13) to Q(-13+21)=Q(8). Hence

W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q)\cong Q(8)^{\oplus r}.

This is exactly the asserted direct-sum statement, including the possible zero direct sum.

claims.proof: The dimension formula is 3g-3+n; substitution gives 18-3+6=21.
claims.statement: The stack M_{6,6} is smooth of complex dimension 21.

claims.proof: This is the weight-26 edge-image statement from the normal-crossings weight spectral sequence, whose positive boundary columns have weights strictly greater than 26.
claims.statement: W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) is the image of H^{26}(\overline M_{6,6};Q) under restriction.

claims.proof: Its degree-26 edge complex is generated by codimension-13 algebraic stable-graph strata decorated by algebraic cotangent classes. These generators are Q(-13), all differentials are algebraic Gysin morphisms between Tate structures, and subquotients of direct sums of Q(-13) are direct sums of Q(-13).
claims.statement: The image in claim ATT-0020-C2 is a direct sum of Q(-13).

claims.proof: Poincare duality identifies it with W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), and Q(-13)(21)=Q(8).
claims.statement: W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) is a direct sum of Q(8).

failed_approaches_addressed.resolution: Not used; degree 26 equals the virtual cohomological dimension.

summary: The weight-26 part of H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) is identified with the image of the degree-26 cohomology of the smooth proper compactification \overline M_{6,6}. Since degree 26 equals twice codimension 13, the relevant image is generated by algebraic boundary-stratum classes and therefore consists of copies of Q(-13). Poincare duality and the dimension-21 twist convert these copies into Q(8).
theorem_statement: The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.
